A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PREAMBLE work and are readable, including appendices A–B in v1 and A–E in v2. The constructions, proofs and existing experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original PRG timing measurements, numerical privacy–communication evaluations and rotation/truncation experiments in Sections 3.3 and 4.1.

after.justification: v2 retains numerical aggregation experiments and adds MNIST/CIFAR-10 training and real-gradient estimation results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core DPF, sampling and validity-proof constructions remain. v2 adds an explicit block-normalization variant, blkscale_B, in Theorems 3.3–3.4 and corrects Gen's initial selector from g0(0) to g1(0). Appendix B and the experiments still describe clipping, so these changes do not establish replacement of experimental preprocessing.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates vector aggregation and cryptographic efficiency without dataset-based learning experiments. v2 adds private image classification on MNIST and CIFAR-10 using CLIP embeddings, plus estimation of gradients collected during CIFAR-10 training.

E2.justification: The Gaussian mechanism and single-trusted-server communication baseline remain the evaluated comparators. The added learning and gradient experiments reuse the Gaussian baseline. Expanded discussion of competing DPF constructions does not introduce head-to-head empirical evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces DP-SGD training protocols with dataset-specific networks, batch sizes, optimization settings and privacy accounting, plus real-gradient estimation and sample-size sweeps. The communication evaluation also changes from two-way cuckoo hashing with roughly 3× overhead to four-way hashing with roughly 1.03× overhead. The earlier PRG timing protocol is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds analysis of training-noise overhead across block and batch sizes, aggregation sensitivity to sample size, and CIFAR-10 checks using different embeddings and batch sizes (Figures 7a, 12 and 15). Real-gradient experiments examine transfer of the synthetic findings. The earlier privacy-budget sweep disappears, while sampling-scheme and truncation comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no explicit repeated-run counts or confidence intervals. v2 reports median learning accuracy with 90% confidence intervals, using ten repetitions for the main MNIST/CIFAR-10 experiments and five for the additional RN50 experiments. These concern newly added experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds learning curves showing accuracy close to the Gaussian baseline at kB = 18,400 for MNIST and 23,000 for the main CIFAR-10 experiment, together with gradient-error, noise-overhead and sample-size results. It removes PRG timing results and the earlier privacy-budget sweep. Revised communication curves use different hashing settings and therefore do not show a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.3–3.4 and Appendix B add formal distortion analysis for random rotations and randomized Hadamard preprocessing, beyond v1's informal discussion and truncation experiments. Existing cryptographic and privacy proofs are largely relocated. The new Hadamard theorem states O(log^2(D)/B), but its displayed appendix proof concludes O(log(D)/sqrt(B)), leaving an internal mismatch.

C1.justification: v2 reframes PREAMBLE as the Euclidean aggregation mechanism built on block-sparse DPFs and explicitly identifies block-sparsity as a contribution. The central sublinear-communication and near-Gaussian privacy–utility claims, including the 64 MB to approximately 1 MB example, remain. Validity proofs and one-hot applications remain despite losing separate contribution bullets.

C2.justification: v2 explains the larger training-noise overhead through additional Renyi subsampling accounting and interprets real-gradient experiments as supporting transfer of the synthetic tradeoffs. Existing qualifications concerning semi-honest servers, cuckoo-hashing failures and incomplete privacy accounting remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds network architecture, CLIP variants, optimizer and scheduler settings, clipping bounds, privacy parameters, accounting software, hardware and epoch timings for the new learning experiments. Conversely, v1's Apple M2/OpenSSL benchmarking details and AES timing breakdown are removed with that study.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 substantially revises positioning against prior cuckoo-hashing constructions and adds detailed comparison with concurrent BGH+25, including equivalence of its big-state scheme to the naive construction and PBC/OKVS tradeoffs. It adds dCP22 and dataset/model references while removing citations associated with the deleted timing benchmark.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the techniques overview, places private aggregation before the construction overview, and creates a dedicated experimental section. Most detailed cryptographic construction and validity-proof material moves into Appendices C–D, with shorter main-text explanations and a revised title and contribution narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 6 consolidates selected communication, truncation and aggregation plots; new learning and gradient figures are added. Construction diagrams move to the appendices, while the earlier complexity summary, PRG-count table and timing plots disappear. Appendix E adds a network-architecture table and reorganized experimental panels.

improvement.justification: The new learning and real-gradient results, repeated-run reporting and detailed experimental settings strengthen evidence for the intended learning application, which v1 supported mainly through numerical aggregation analysis. The benefit is tempered by removal of the cryptographic timing study and the new Hadamard theorem/proof rate mismatch, limiting the overall quality gain.
